intent: Name the page, or the section of it, that the header heads.
typical_uses: The name of the object a page shows, such as a customer or an order
The name of a section under the page's own header, as an h2

dont_use_when.situation: The headline of a placeholder with nothing to show

invariants.text: PageHeaderTitle renders an h1, unless `render` substitutes another element, which keeps the title's class and props.
The title stays on one line and truncates with an ellipsis when its column runs out of room; its browser heading margins are cleared.
`typography` picks the ramp role - Heading 1 (20/28) for `heading`, the Page Title role (26/32) for `display` - whatever the header's `size`.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave every header on the page an h1
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `render={<h2 />}` to the title of every header below the page's own, so the page has one h1

render.states: render replaces the rendered h1 with an element the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (PageHeaderTitle passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the heading level, such as `render={<h2 />}` for a section's header.

good.title: A section's title, one level under the page's own
An object's name in the Page Title role

bad.title: Two headers on one page, both titled with an h1
bad.why: The section's title is an h1 as well, so the outline has two top-level headings and the section no longer reads as part of the page; it takes `render={<h2 />}`.
